channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Joey Porter DAL Cornerback

Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

This was the expected outcome. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that Ferguson will likely be out for “multiple weeks” after suffering a knee injury. He was already dealing with an ankle injury when it happened. Ferguson does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Cowboys ruled out Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Tyler Goodson DAL Running Back

The Cowboys will be without their No. 2 running back, removing what little threat there was to Javonte Williams’ workload. Goodson should remain stashed on 12-team benches if possible, though he could miss next week as well.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Trent Williams (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Trent Williams SF Tackle

Williams evidently injured his shoulder during the 49ers’ practice on Thursday, as did LB Dre Greenlaw (knee). 49ers OT Vederian Lowe would be Williams’ replacement if he cannot play. 49ers starting perimeter CBs Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot), and slot DB Upton Stout (shoulder) are also questionable.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Losing Evans for this one is a bummer. The 49ers’ and Cowboys’ offenses should facilitate a high-scoring game environment. Regardless, the 49ers are smartly prioritizing Evans’ long-term health. Whenever he returns, he is likely to be full-go. Keep him stashed on fantasy football benches.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez had three limited sessions ahead of this week and, should the Jaguars bludgeon the Titans, would profile to get some between-the-tackles work with Bhayshul Tuten dealing with ankle and foot injuries and not getting in much practice time. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against Tennessee.

item.title: Cardinals ruled out Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) for Week 10 against the Rams.
item.description:
Hjalte Froholdt ARI Offensive Lineman

The Cardinals will be without Froholdt, their starting center, against a Rams team that is likely to rely on its ground game and ascending defense while navigating pass-catcher injuries. This makes life a little harder for rookie QB Carson Beck, who will make his first NFL start this week.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Chris Brooks GB Running Back

Brooks would have a chance to assume passing-down duties if he is activated off injured reserve. That would probably quash Pierre Strong’s value more than Marshawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson’s, but Brooks would probably be the favorite to see the most snaps among Green Bay’s runners if active. It would be a rough FLEX play against a good Vikings defense.

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 11 assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slowplayed his return and have been rewarded as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Charles Cross (ankle) won’t play in Seattle’s Week 10 game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Charles Cross SEA Tackle

He did resume practicing on Thursday, but it was a quick hook and a Friday DNP. Still, it’s an encouraging sign for his status for Week 12 — after the Week 11 bye — that he was able to get on the practice field at all.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

He’ll return to his boom/bust fantasy role as Seattle’s field-stretcher and punt returner after missing a few weeks due to this knee injury. Shaheed practiced in full all week and should not have any real limitations.

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

item.title: Omar Cooper (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. The team listed him as questionable for a reason, but he is likely on the right side of questionable at this time. With Adonai Mitchell (knee) suddenly ailing, Cooper could warrant WR3 treatment against the Bills.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell practiced in full today, but was added to the injury report with a new knee issue. This is a little concerning. The team could be trying to collect more info right now. We expect to hear more later today or at some point tomorrow. At this point, Mitchell must be viewed as firmly in the questionable column.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful for Miami’s Week 10 game against the Colts.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

He did not practice Thursday or Friday after aggravating his surgically repaired knee in practice on Wednesday. The Dolphins have no reason to push Bell, so we’d be stunned if he played. Not that you were looking for reasons to lean into a Kyle McCord start, but Bell’s injury should free up targets for Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas on the FLEX line.

item.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play. Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Carson Wentz (ankle) is not on Minnesota’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

He’ll be Kirk Cousins’ QB2 on Sunday. Those of us who watched Monday’s game against the Bills are very grateful for that.

item.title: Kyler Murray (hamstring) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

He wouldn’t have played anyway with Kirk Cousins coming over. Murray will reclaim QB2 duties when healthy, but dealing with a grade 2 strain on his hamstring, that may not be for a few weeks.

item.title: Jauan Jennings (calf) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings would have been useful additional depth to have with Jordan Addison suddenly questionable. Tai Felton will likely see more work in Week 10, and perhaps Odell Beckham Jr. will be elevated off the practice squad if Jordan Addison (thumb) also sits.

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) is not on the Bills’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Jets.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are both good to go this weekend. Bills RT Spencer Brown (ankle) is unfortunately doubtful to play. Overall, the Bills’ offensive line health is trending in the right direction, though. Bills CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable.

Source: Chris Brown

item.title: Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

Kevin O’Connell described it as Addison getting “dinged” in practice today. Not ideal. Addison would have been in for a workload bump with T.J. Hockenson out, as it stands it looks like Kirk Cousins will just throw to Justin Jefferson 25 times like it’s 2022 again.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson didn’t practice at any point this week and his status for Week 11 is likely in question as well. Gavin Bartholomew has picked up the slack this year when Hockenson has sat and will be a reasonable low-end TE2 play.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) is not on the Bills’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

With Kincaid’s multi-year knee injury behind him, the Bills’ tight end put together a great offseason and has proven to be a reliable player even when banged up this season. Kincaid is firmly in the TE1 ranks for this divisional showdown against the Jets in Week 10.

Source: Chris Brown

item.title: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Danielle Hunter HOU Defensive End

Hunter popped up on the report with this injury on Thursday as limited and wound up ruled out after a DNP on Friday. Rough scenes for the $40 million-a-year edge rusher. This will be the first game he has missed since the 2021 season. Houston’s pass rush looks tenuous against the Browns with Will Anderson Jr. also on the questionable line.

item.title: Will Anderson (ankle) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Will Anderson HOU Defensive End

Anderson was added to the report as limited on Thursday and did not practice on Friday, throwing his status into major doubt ahead of Houston’s game in Cleveland. He has been listed with an ankle before this year, and with Danielle Hunter suddenly out, Cleveland’s pass offense could see some efficiency boosts against the Texans without their star rushers.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

item.title: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

The diminutive speedster got in back-to-back full practices and should see a reasonable workload against the Browns. He’s a low-end WR3 or high-end FLEX play at this point, with more upside possible if he’s able to repeat last week’s target share.

item.title: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

Montgomery got in a full practice for the first time since returning from his groin injury. It’s certainly possible he’s back, but given a likely snap count in his return, it’d be hard to trust him as more than a what-the-heck FLEX.

item.title: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Woody Marks HOU Running Back

Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

item.title: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Peter Skoronski TEN Guard

Not exactly what the Titans needed, losing their best offensive lineman ahead of hosting the division leaders, but it’s what they’ll get. Skoronski should be considered questionable for Week 11 as well after not practicing at any point this week following Tennessee’s Week 9 bye.

item.title: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Andrei Iosivas CIN Wide Receiver

Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

If Spears can play, this is theoretically the kind of blowout game script that sets him up for FLEX value via PPR scam. We wouldn’t advise chasing it, but we wouldn’t be surprised if it happened. Spears got in a full practice today, which would seem to leave him on the optimistic side of questionable.

item.title: Chiefs ruled out RT Jaylon Moore (concussion) for Week 10 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jaylon Moore KC Offensive Lineman

Moore will unfortunately miss this weekend’s game against the Falcons, who field a capable defensive tackle unit. Atlanta has not defended the run well, though, so the Chiefs should be able to get by without him. Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is questionable to play.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

Patrick Mahomes will have his speedy wide receiver on the field this weekend. Unfortunately for Worthy, he may be operating in a reduced role with Josh Downs now in Kansas City. Worthy can still be rostered in 12-team formats, but his play could be even more volatile.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Not much of a surprise after he sat out Friday with what Andy Reid called a “tight groin.” This has officially waded into “we’ll see” territory over the weekend. Emmett Johnson would be a low-end RB1 with a good workload if Walker is ruled out ahead of Sunday’s games.

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
item.description:
Blake Corum

Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Alvin Kamara (back) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

As usual, Kamara’s back listing has not prevented him in any real way from playing. A potential Travis Etienne activation off injured reserve could cut into his FLEX value in Week 10, but if Etienne stays on IR, Kamara will be a reasonable play against a rough Panthers run defense.

item.title: Derrick Harmon (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 10 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Derrick Harmon PIT Defensive Tackle

He got in a full practice on Friday and spoke with reporters as well. Based on that, we’d guess he’s got a good chance to be activated off injured reserve and play against the Bengals in the first week of his 21-day window.

item.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) is not on Pittsburgh’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Ben Skowronek PIT Wide Receiver

We’ll see if he goes back to being a thorn in the ceiling cases for the remainder of the Steelers’ offensive players against the Bengals. Skowronek has no standalone value.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers will be in line for a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans. The good news is that the over/under has climbed to 46.5 after last week’s date with Joey Fagnano, leaving Meyers as a more viable touchdown threat in Week 10 than he was in a limited passing workload against the Ravens.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

He practiced on Friday in a limited session, and as it was last week, he’s active despite not much actual work in a move that signals the Jaguars are clearly just trying to get their lead back some rest. He’ll be an upside RB2 against the Titans.

item.title: Eagles released OT Fred Johnson.
item.description:
Fred Johnson

Johnson is a decent bet to receive interest via the waiver wire. He has played for the Eagles since 2023, logging 1,589 offensive and special teams snaps combined. While he primarily contributed as a traditional tackle, the Eagles would at times line him up as an extra blocker at tight end. He is not a reliable starter, but can still contribute in the right situation.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson is expected to be out for a couple of weeks, though the Rams are fortuitously on bye in Week 11. The rest of the Rams’ tight ends are in varying states of health. Colby Parkinson (ribs) will likely play through his injury again. Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice on Thursday. Their game status has not been revealed.

Source: Zach Edwards

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

The Rams were optimistic about McDuffie practicing on Thursday and playing on Sunday. The former did not happen. It sounds like he has a chance to play this weekend, but his recovery appears to be going slightly slower than expected. Rams S Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable to play, though LG Steve Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out.

Source: Zach Edwards

item.title: Myles Garrett (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that he expects Garrett to play. This is unfortunate news for the Cardinals, who will be led by rookie Carson Beck in his first NFL start. Garrett played very well last week against the Commanders, but his preseason knee issue is apparently still bothering him. Hopefully, he can get healthy before the season’s end.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) return timeline has not changed.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

A few days ago, McVay told reporters that Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve due to transaction limitations, so it was a bit surprising to see him land there yesterday. The move prompted some concern. He was initially expected to return in Week 14 or 15, and he will officially be eligible to return on the latter date against the Cowboys. As of today, he is on track to do so, just in time for the fantasy football playoffs. Nacua should not be dropped in any format. He will be a WR1 upon returning.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

He did practice again today, finally hitting a full session, so he at least has cleared a full week of practices if nothing else. If Etienne does play he could be a reasonable FLEX option. There are reports that he could be on a snap count if he does play, and that mixes with the early-season usage to create a situation that isn’t necessarily guaranteed to smash. That said, the Panthers are an enticing matchup.

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Reid added “we’ll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow.” Not exactly a glowing endorsement for Walker playing, though we expect the injury report later today to at least read questionable. If Walker were unable to go, Emmett Johnson would probably find himself with a low-end RB1 workload against the Falcons.

Source: Sam McDowell

item.title: Tailese Fuaga (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

Fuaga has a knee sprain, per Kellen Moore. It sounds like a short-term thing and Moore has said he won’t need to go on injured reserve. Asim Richards and Mason Murphy are the backup tackles and Richards played left tackle while Kelvin Banks was sidelined earlier this season.

Source: Katherine Terrell

item.title: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

The passing-down blocking back’s absence should create more opportunities for Alvin Kamara and, possibly, Travis Etienne in the passing game.

Source: Matthew Paras

item.title: Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

He made it back on to the practice field on Friday, so he’s probably on the optimistic side of questionable at this point. Todd Monken did say at his Friday presser that Boston is “trending in the right direction.” Boston did miss the first two sessions of the week but has been no stranger to the injury report this year and has tended to gut it out. Boston was seen wearing a walking boot as he left the locker room. He still has a chance to play, but his status is worth monitoring closely.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice all week and enters Atlanta’s Week 11 bye off two completely lost weeks. The rookie hasn’t made much of an impact so far and doesn’t necessarily need to be kept on rosters in non-dynasty leagues at this point.

item.title: James Pearce Jr. (back) is questionable for Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

Pearce got in two limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday’s practice. He would appear to be on the optimistic side of questionable.

item.title: Jordan Schultz reports the Eagles are waiving WR Hollywood Brown.
item.description:
Marquise Brown

The trade market did not materialize for Mr. Brown, who has eight targets in four active games with the Eagles this year. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere down the stretch.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Cardinals signed TE Elijah Higgins to a three-year extension worth “up to” $26.8 million.
item.description:
Elijah Higgins ARI Tight End

Just weeks after earning a rare blurb from us here at Rotoworld, Higgins followed up his blurb-worthy performance with a three-year extension. The 26-year-old tight end has caught 18 passes for 162 yards and one touchdown this season, and is a year removed from the 30-301-0 line he posted last year. With the Cardinals hurting at receiver, it’s possible Higgins could see an expanded role going forward, especially after signing this deal, which can net him up to $26.8 million.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

He practiced on Friday and, as it was last week, the Jaguars cleared him with just one practice. He’ll be an upside RB2 against the Titans.

item.title: Cardinals signed TE Elijah Higgins to a three-year, extension.
item.description:
Elijah Higgins ARI Tight End

Just weeks after earning a rare blurb from us here at Rotoworld, Higgins followed up his blurb-worthy performance with a three-year extension. The 26-year-old tight end has caught 18 passes for 162 yards and one touchdown this season, and is a year removed from the 30-301-0 line he posted last year. With the Cardinals hurting at receiver, it’s possible Higgins could see an expanded role going forward, especially after signing this deal, which can net him up to $26.8 million.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Bam Knight will play in Week 10 against the Rams after clearing concussion protocol.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday, Knight is officially off of the injury report and good to go for Sunday’s game against the Rams. Both Knight and Tyler Allgeier are expected to factor heavily into the Cardinals’ running game this weekend, especially with Carson Beck making his first career start with a depleted receiving corps. Both Knight and Allgeier will be fringe RB3/Flex plays in a game that could prove tough for the Cardinals’ banged-up offense.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Xavier Legette (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

Legette has missed the past six games but could join the active squad for the first time since Week 2. Even if he returns this week, the third-year wideout may have trouble carving out a fantasy-relevant receiving role every week behind Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble, and running back Chuba Hubbard. However, even in this crowded picture, the 25-year-old could warrant a stash in some deep leagues for those craving anyone with upside at wide receiver. His added presence could help Bryce Young’s fantasy value as the season goes on.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (core) is doubtful for Week 10 against the Saints.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks was previously listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, only for head coach Dave Canales to announce on Friday that Brooks was working with the scout team, not the 53-man roster, meaning he was actually limited throughout the week. After logging three limited practices, Brooks appears unlikely to play in Week 10 given the doubtful designation. With his return window opened earlier this week, the Panthers could delay his return by two more weeks before having to either rule him out for the season or activate him from injured reserve. We will see how things go for him next week ahead of Week 11’s game against the Ravens.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Israel Abanikanda will serve as the team’s RB2 in Week 10 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Israel Abanikanda DAL Running Back

Abanikanda will get the practice squad elevation over Kendre Miller, who recently signed with the team after being released by the Saints. Abanikanda has spent part of the last two seasons with the Cowboys and had a solid preseason, rushing for 91 scoreless yards on 22 carries while adding three receptions for 16 yards. We wouldn’t expect Abanikanda to see enough meaningful work to be fantasy relevant this week but he could be worth a stash in deeper leagues as insurance for Javonte Williams.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, will make the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

Despite some belief that Stevenson could miss a short period of time due to a knee injury he suffered late in Week 9’s loss to the Packers, the 28-year-old back will have an outside chance at suiting up against the Lions after logging back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Backup Corey Kiner is expected to step into an expanded role if Stevenson is unable to go, but will be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/FLEX play if Stevenson does suit up. With the Pats and Lions set to face off at 9:30 AM EST in Germany, fantasy managers will want to check early inactives before setting their lineups if they either player on their roster.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Assuming all goes well, Cooper will likely be removed from the injury report before the end of the day, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Bills. Cooper caught eight passes for 58 yards in Week 9’s loss to the Chiefs, but that was with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. While we wouldn’t expect another 11-target outing from Cooper with Wilson expected to be active for Week 10, he could have some FLEX appeal after yet another strong showing. We will check back in with a final status update on Cooper when the team announces it later in the day.

Source: Zack Rosenblatt

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is “confident” that Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Glenn said Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league’s concussion protocol. Wilson missed last week’s game against the Chiefs due to his brain injury, but has practiced in a limited capacity twice this week and is trending toward a return. We will get a final update on Wilson once he has officially cleared the protocol, but fantasy managers can start him as a mid-to-high-end WR2 in a game that could feature plenty of points against a high-powered Bills offense.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Jordan Davis will not play in Week 10 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jordan Davis

Neither Davis nor recently acquired safety Jessie Bates had bye weeks with their previous teams, which Coen noted when announcing that the two players would be sidelined for Week 10. The decision to sit both players will essentially give them a “bye week,” and it conveniently comes in a week when the Jaguars face an inferior opponent in Tennessee. Both players should be good to go in Week 11 when the Jaguars visit the Giants.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter released a statement saying Lamar Jackson (thumb) will be out for the next 6-10 weeks.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

On the short end of this timeline, Jackson could return in Week 16 against the Browns. On the long end, Jackson would be looking at returning around the Wild Card or Divisional Round of the playoffs if the Ravens make the postseason. This timeline closely aligns with the 6-9 week absence NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier in the week. If this isn’t a season-ender for Lamar, it will be close, and how the Ravens perform over the next several weeks with Jacoby Brissett under center will likely determine whether the Ravens dress him for the final few weeks of the season, even if he is ready to go. Minter said that Jackson is “doing well” after suffering his injury in Week 8 against the Bills, which is encouraging, but we’re a long way from knowing if a return for Jackson is truly in the cards. The 4-5 Ravens have lost their last four games but hope to turn things around on Monday night when they play host to the Chargers.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Falcons signed CB C.J. Henderson to a two-year extension.
item.description:
C.J. Henderson ATL Cornerback

The former 2020 first-rounder can earn up to $20 million on his new deal, per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, with $11 million being guaranteed. Henderson was drafted No. 9 overall by the Jaguars in 2020, but has since bounced around to the Panthers, Texans, and Steelers, and was actually cut by the Falcons in August 2025 during final roster cutdowns after camp. Since then, Henderson has played his way not only onto the 53-man roster, but into a starting role. He has started six of the eight games he has appeared in for Atlanta this season, totaling 41 tackles, nine pass breakups, and one fumble recovery while earning a PFF coverage grade of 65.3. Playing almost exclusively on the outside, he has allowed opposing receivers to go for 252 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Falcons signed DE Cameron Thomas to a three-year contract extension.
item.description:
Cameron Thomas ATL Defensive End

Thomas has started all nine games he has appeared in for the Falcons this season. The 26-year-old lineman spent the previous two seasons in Cleveland with head coach Kevin Stefanski, and then joined Stefanski in Atlanta on a one-year deal this offseason. Thomas has totaled 25 tackles, two sacks, and one TFL this season for the Falcons, earning a PFF grade of 77.2. His deal is worth up to $33 million and he will now be under contract through the 2029 season.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers was clearly not a point of emphasis in a game expected to carry significant weather impacts. Despite the weather subsiding in the second half, McCarthy remained fixed on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets. The matchup also played a role in the game plan, with the Commanders missing numerous key linebackers while blitzing at an above average rate. Nabers is in a good spot to bounce back against the Jaguars in Week 11, where he’ll return to WR1 status in fantasy circles.

item.title: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Malachi Fields NYG Wide Receiver

The New York wide receivers were clearly limited by a game plan to feature tight end Isaiah Likely, with the starting trio of Malik Nabers, Fields, and Darnell Mooney combining for just 10 receptions, one more than the nine of Likely. Even so, Fields continued to demonstrate a strong connection with quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the rookie finished second on the team in receiving despite seeing only four targets. The highlight of the game came in the second half when McCarthy threaded a ball over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline for a 25-yard gain to Fields. Although his weekly volume likely won’t be vast enough to return consistent fantasy production without an injury to Nabers or Likely, Fields continues to show the growth dynasty managers were hoping for.

item.title: Isaiah Likely caught 9-of-11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely as clearly the going-in game plan in a game expected to be heavily influenced by weather. The rain cleared in the first half but Likely remained the featured option through the air, likely influenced by heavy blitz rates and unrelenting pressure from the Washington defense. The 11-target game was the fifth time this season that the veteran tight end hit double-digit targets but the first time doing so with J.J. McCarthy under center. Likely remains a surefire TE1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Jaguars in Week 11.

item.title: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 44 yards on three receptions.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Skattebo immediately returned to a workhorse role following the shortcomings of Devin Singletary in Week 10, the latter of whom saw but one opportunity to the 22 of Skattebo. The Skatt-man bookended halftime with a score from one yard out on the team’s final possession of the first half and a score from 13 yards out on the team’s first possession of the second half, earning two backflips in the process. The second-year back also escaped down the sideline for a 34-yard reception in the first quarter to pad his counting stats. Despite the resurgence in workload, Skattebo will be a borderline FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 11.

item.title: J.J. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 24-21, Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 34 yards on six carries.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

McCarthy appeared to be in complete control throughout before a game-sealing interception with under a minute to play in a three-point game. He demonstrated plus pocket presence and made numerous dime-worthy throws, the most impressive of which was a 25-yard dart to rookie Malachi Fields that was put in the only place where Fields could come down with the ball, over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline. McCarthy leaned heavily on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets in what appeared to be a matchup-based game plan in the face of an aggressive pass rush. The Giants fall to 5-3-1 with the loss and pass the first tie-breaker to the Commanders after the two teams’ tie earlier this season. The Giants get a difficult matchup against arguably the most well-rounded roster in the AFC when they host the Jaguars in Week 11, where McCarthy falls to a mid-range QB2 in fantasy circles.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs and the Washington pass offense went as Jayden Daniels went, with the dual threat quarterback mixing perfectly thrown passes with completely errant ones, two of which were directed toward Diggs. A third incompletion bounced off Diggs’ helmet as the veteran receiver should have drawn a defensive pass interference penalty, with the ball eventually ruled an incompletion upon further review after Treylon Burks appeared to come down with what would have been one of the wilder receptions of the season. Daniels’ best pass of the game came on the game-winning touchdown to Diggs in the flat on a crosser, threaded between two defenders. Diggs made a third miss as he took it into the end zone from 32 yards out to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games behind the Giants with the first tie-breaker in hand. He will remain a volatile WR3 on capped routes against the Bengals in Week 11.

item.title: Austin Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 26 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

The veteran in-season addition’s 13 opportunities matched that of starter Rachaad White, the latter of whom played the team’s first two drives before splitting the workload the rest of the way. Ekeler also split red zone work, although it was White that nearly missed a touchdown on a seven-yard run that was tackled at the one in the second quarter. Either way, the near-even split between the two caps the fantasy upside of both backs in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with neither on the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

item.title: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 47 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding five yards on one reception.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

White started in name only, playing the first two drives before splitting backfield duties with fellow veteran Austin Ekeler for the remainder of the game. The two backs ended with the same number of opportunities while also splitting red zone work, with White narrowly missing a touchdown in the second quarter on his second longest run of the evening, a seven-yard scamper up the gut that was stopped at the one. His lone explosive run went for 18 yards, with those two carries accounting for more than 50 percent of his yardage total on the ground. White has fallen into a strict timeshare in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt and brings little fantasy upside ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

item.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Commanders’ 24-21, Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 28 yards on 10 carries.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

A late second quarter touchdown drive that was sparked by a long reception by veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs was capped off by tight end Ben Sinnott’s first touchdown of the season to send the Commanders into the half with a three-point lead. The two sides would trade touchdowns in the third quarter before the wheels appeared to fall off for Washington, with their first three possessions of the final frame going turnover on downs, interception, and interception, allowing the Giants to nurse a four-point lead inside the two-minute warning. Daniels drove the field in 49 seconds on just three plays, connecting with Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining. The Commanders would escape on the backs of a Rasul Douglas interception to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games back of the Giants and with the first tie-breaker in hand following the previous tie. Daniels will look to keep the momentum going in a Week 11 meeting with the surging Bengals, where he will be an upside QB1 in another must-win game.

item.title: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Vega Ioane BAL Guard

The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Bam Knight (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

Knight is on track to resume his lead rushing role this week. Unfortunately, the Cardinals face the Seahawks, potentially rendering Knight a touchdown-dependent FLEX starter against their elite defense. Hopefully, Knight remains setback-free for the rest of the week.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.

Source: San Francisco 49ers

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

At this point, Evans seems like a long shot to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys. The 49ers allowed Christian McCaffrey to try to play through his Achilles tendinitis and it did not go well. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan indicated they learned from the experience and will let Evans get fully healthy before allowing him to retake the field.

Source: San Francisco 49ers

item.title: Charles Cross (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Charles Cross SEA Tackle

Cross and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) were both limited at today’s practice, giving them a chance to play on Sunday against the Cardinals. Seahawks stud DT Leonard Williams (stinger) remains sidelined.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Giants declared CB Paulson Adebo, OT J.C. Davis, OL Josh Sills, CB Nikko Reed, DT C.J. Okoye, TE Thomas Fidone and OLB Malik Harrison inactive for Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Paulson Adebo NYG Cornerback

The Giants are seemingly demoting Adebo, who entered the season as one of the team’s top-three cornerbacks. Colton Hood will take his place. Aside from that, Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and J.J. McCarthy (hip) are good to go tonight, in what is expected to be a rainy Thursday Night Football game.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Commanders declared QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Isaac Yiadom, DT Ricky Barber, G Tanoa Togiai, C Lucas Patrick and TE Colson Yankoff inactive for Week 10 against the Giants.
item.description:
Isaac Yiadom WAS Cornerback

Among the Commanders’ players who are currently healthy enough to practice, most of them will play. Treylon Burks (foot) could end up being a decoy, but Chig Okonkwo (hip) should be good to go. Only Yiadom and a few others are unable to go on Thursday night, though tonight’s kickoff could be delayed by weather.

Source: Washington Commanders

item.title: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell should be good to go for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game against the Ravens. He and Omarion Hampton seemingly put a little distance between Kimani Vidal in the second half last week, though Mitchell only makes for a shaky bench stash.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku is not worth rostering whenever he officially returns to the active roster, but he theoretically can contribute offensively. He will likely be a mildly productive member of the Chargers’ three-player tight end rotation.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

item.title: Ben Sinnott caught all four targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
item.description:
Ben Sinnott WAS Tight End

Sinnott entered the game with just one reception this season while playing as the primary blocking tight end alongside Chig Okonkwo. Okonkwo departed in the second quarter with a back injury and returned to start the second half, with the time off the field paving the way for Sinnott to triple his year-to-date reception total and score his first touchdown of the season. He would add one reception in the second half to push his total to four. The touchdown reception also came with a bit of intrigue as the pass appeared to be targeting Stefon Diggs in the end zone. Sinnott was on a crossing route at the goal line and happened to cross paths at the perfect time. He will not be fantasy viable for as long as Okonkwo remains healthy.

item.title: Antonio Williams caught both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

Williams cashed in on his first target of the game for a 31-yard score in the third quarter, adding one additional grab for 11 yards in the final frame. The electric rookie continues to play starters snaps and challenge for the team lead in route rate but had yet to get completely on the same page with quarterback Jayden Daniels, the latter of whom leaned heavily on Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo in this one. The talent is undeniable for Williams, but fantasy managers would love to see a bump in targets before feeling comfortable entering him into starting lineups. Williams’ next chance to return a usable fantasy outing comes in Week 11 against the inside-funnel Bengals, where he should avoid the primary coverage of lockdown corner DJ Turner.

item.title: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

Harris led the team with seven targets last week, catching just three of them for six yards. Although he is not fantasy-relevant on his own, his presence theoretically helps Justin Herbert and Harris is on track to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

The back spasms that sidelined McConkey in Week 9 against the Texans evidently remain an issue. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 10’s Thursday Night Football game. The rest of the receiving corps is too unreliable for a WR3-level pivot if he is unable to play.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

Wentz is tentatively on track to be available for backup duties. Kyler Murray (hamstring) remains sidelined. Neither Vikings quarterback needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson still has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Packers, but at this point, it seems likely that he will miss at least one game. Hockenson’s potential absence would likely allow Jordan Addison to earn a little more work than he has in recent weeks. Stay tuned.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Source: Dallas Cowboys

item.title: Joey Porter (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Joey Porter DAL Cornerback

Porter reportedly told reporters that his “whole foot is jacked up.” That sounds bad. He was able to run today, and hadn’t in a while, but declined to say whether he will play in Week 10 against the 49ers. We suspect he will sit out this weekend’s contest.

Source: Jane Slater

item.title: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

Source: Zac Jackson

item.title: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

Dell is firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns. He led the team with nine targets last week, catching four passes for 105 yards and one touchdown. The coaching staff reportedly drew up a play just to get him over the century mark. He is a FLEX starter this week.

Source: Zac Jackson

item.title: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

This morning, Boston told reporters that he was hoping to resume practicing today. Unfortunately, he was unable to do so. That said, Boston’s toe injury is feeling better and things are “trending up” at the moment. It sounds like the rookie wide receiver has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Texans and would be a WR3/FLEX if so.

Source: Zac Jackson

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Chris Bell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

The Dolphins were regularly limiting Bell’s practice reps earlier this season, so this may just be routine maintenance. The rookie wide receiver was limited yesterday. Bell has not yet established himself as a fantasy-relevant player, and he is unlikely to do so in Kyle McCord’s first start, especially if his surgically repaired knee is bothering him.

Source: Miami Dolphins

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

Yesterday, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that the Rams were hopeful that McDuffie would play in Week 10 against the Cardinals. He is tentatively on track to do so with today’s return to practice. The Rams will potentially morph into a run-heavy team that relies on the defense to generate turnovers with their top-two wide receivers and top tight end sidelined. McDuffie can help them accomplish that.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Back-to-back limited sessions have us believing Cooper has a good chance to play in Week 10 against the Bills. The role has been up-and-down as the Jets struggle to work in all their weapons. Cooper qualifies as a FLEX play against what has been a shaky Bills defense when not facing Carson Wentz this season.

item.title: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

Source: New Orleans Football

item.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was limited at today’s practice. He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

After two limited sessions we don’t have a lot of doubt that Kincaid will be ready to play in Week 10’s game against the Jets. He may be managed a bit, though, as he toughs it out. He’ll remain a TE1 play regardless.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez played through the hand injury without issue last week, totaling 10 carries and two receptions on Thursday night. He should again handle a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans in Week 10, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) managing something.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Jared Goff DET Quarterback

That should alleviate any concern that he’d miss Sunday morning’s Munich kickoff against the Patriots. Goff will be a low-end QB1 for that one assuming no major negative news hits on Friday.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten sat out all three practices before playing in last week’s Thursday Night Football game, totaling 12 carries in the process. We tentatively expect him to play in Week 10 against the Titans, and he should be in fantasy football lineups even if he sits out or is limited on Friday. Stay tuned.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

He played through this last week, managing an 8/86 line against the Dolphins. We’d be surprised if he wasn’t removed from the injury report tomorrow after getting in two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday.

item.title: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

He did not travel to Munich with the team and has not practiced since injuring his ankle in Week 8. Juice Scruggs will continue to fill in at center.

item.title: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
D.J. Reed DET Cornerback

Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

item.title: Kerby Joseph (knee) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Kerby Joseph DET Safety

Joseph got in a full practice session with the Lions on Thursday, but will not travel to Munich with the club. It sounds like he’ll have a real chance to play in Week 11 when the Lions head back to the states.

item.title: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Peter Skoronski TEN Guard

The Titans’ starting left guard is very unlikely to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, who field a top-tier defense. Skoronski has been sidelined since injuring his hamstring in Week 8 against the Bengals.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Post-Week 9 reports had Stevenson with a chance to miss a short period of time, but a limited session at least points to the idea that he could play in Munich on Sunday morning. Fantasy managers reliant on Stevenson or dabbling with Corey Kiner will want to keep an eye on Friday’s injury report.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (back) is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Giants.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo was accompanied by trainers to the locker room after failing to play on a three-and-out possession in the second quarter against the Giants. The team deemed him questionable to return before the subsequent possession. Okonkwo caught both targets for 17 yards prior to departing.

item.title: Giants declared CB Paulson Adebo, OT J.C. Davis, OL Josh Sills, CB Nikko Reed, DT C.J. Okoye, TE Thomas Fidone and OLB Malik Harrison inactive for Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Paulson Adebo NYG Cornerback

The Giants are seemingly demoting Adebo, who entered the season and one of the team’s top-three cornerbacks. Colton Hood will take his place. Aside from that, Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and J.J. McCarthy (hip) are good to go tonight, in what is expected to be a rainy Thursday Night Football game.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears was listed as a limited participant on today’s injury report, theoretically giving him a chance to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars’ elite run defense. Spears’ potential return could lower Tony Pollard’s snap share a tad, though Spears does not need to be rostered in 10-team leagues.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Two limited practices would seem to have him with a real chance to play in Munich, and the fact that he made the trip at all makes it seem likely he’ll have a real chance to go. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice report.

item.title: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: James Pearce Jr. (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP for the 23-year-old. Pearce Jr. will probably at least hit the questionable line on Friday and has a chance to be cleared off altogether if things trend in the right direction. Kevin Stefanski did not seem overly concerned about his status when asked about it, saying the Falcons “also want him to get healthy and feel good.”

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

item.title: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

Source: https://www.panthers.com/team/injury-report/

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Woody Marks HOU Running Back

Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said to “expect a lot of Cam Skattebo” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

The Giants host the Commanders for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. The open-air stadium is currently experiencing heavy rain, and Fowler indicates the rainfall will continue this evening. Devin Singletary will back up Skattebo, but the touch distribution will heavily “slant” toward Skattebo, solidifying his status as an RB2.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: David Montgomery (groin) returned to practice on Thursday.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

Montgomery was mostly working out with a trainer, but DeMeco Ryans said they were “pleased with the progress he was making.” It’s possible this goes down as a DNP still on the official report, but it is real progress that he’s back on the field and he now has a non-zero chance to suit up for Week 10.

Source: Jon M. Alexander

item.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Luke Musgrave (neck) “probably” will not play in 2026.
item.description:
Luke Musgrave GB Tight End

Earlier this season, the Packers thought that Musgrave had a chance to return. Unfortunately, it appears as though that is no longer the case. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Musgrave’s “tenure with the Packers is all but over.”

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes the Packers should not sign MarShawn Lloyd to an extension after next season.
item.description:
MarShawn Lloyd GB Running Back

Schneidman believes it is “not possible” to sign Lloyd to an extension after the 2027 season because of the young running back’s poor play. Lloyd is still trying to beat defenders around the edge with speed, rather than running north-south when he needs to. Although the injuries are mostly behind him, he has failed to live up to preseason expectations. Lloyd does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the forseeable future.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Former Bucs head coach Bruce Arians says he has “the itch” to coach football again.
item.description:
Bruce Arians

Arians detailed myriad health issues that he dealt with in his final season as the Bucs’ head coach. He tore his Achilles and eventually injured his back. Arians was also monitoring an aneurysm in his heart at the time. He stepped away from coaching after the 2021 season but remained with the Bucs in an advisory role for some time. Arians won 13 games in his final season as a head coach and took home the Lombardi Trophy in his penultimate season. Now 74 years old, Arians wouldn’t be the long-term answer for a team, but he could be an option for a team in a win-now window. He later stated that he would consider returning to the Bucs and is only interested in a head-coaching role.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Andrei Iosivas CIN Wide Receiver

Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve, though he practiced in full today. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

item.title: Ravens signed K Harrison Mevis to their practice squad.
item.description:
Harrison Mevis BAL Kicker

The team added Riley Patterson to their active roster yesterday, but both kickers will likely have a chance to earn the job in practice this week. We aren’t expecting great fantasy numbers from either kicker with Lamar Jackson no longer fueling the offense.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Broncos have revoked their trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley because of a failed physical.
item.description:
Daiyan Henley LAC Linebacker

The move, or lack thereof, was announced by Denver around midnight, and Rapoport later gave the reasoning. Henley has been playing through a knee issue for multiple weeks, though he has also dealt with other injuries that could have caused the Broncos to back out. Denver originally agreed to give fourth- and fifth-round picks to acquire Henley. He will now return to the Chargers. As Rapoport points out, the 0-8 Chargers now officially made zero trades ahead of the deadline.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Deommodore Lenoir (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Deommodore Lenoir SF Defensive Back

Lenoir and Renardo Green (back) were among the two 49ers cornerbacks not practicing on Wednesday. Fellow cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) was a limited participant. With the slew of secondary injuries, the Cowboys wideouts will have an easier chance at chunk gains against San Francisco for Week 10.

item.title: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Leonard Williams SEA Defensive Tackle

Williams missed last week due to a stinger and continues to be sidelined. He will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at playing in Week 10 against the Raiders.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed has missed the last two weeks with a knee injury, but he was able to practice in full to open Week 10. A full practice participation is a good sign we’ll see Shaheed on the field for Week 10 against the Raiders. He has been splitting WR2 opportunities with Cooper Kupp this year and belongs on fantasy benches until further notice.

item.title: Charles Cross (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Charles Cross SEA Tackle

Cross remains sidelined with a high ankle sprain he suffered in Week 7. He is yet to return to practice and therefore is trending towards missing Week 10 against the Raiders; a full practice participation would be needed to feel confident about his chances of playing this week.

item.title: Travon Walker (rib) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Travon Walker

Walker suffered a rib injury in practice last week but played through it in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
