item.title: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Commanders listed Treylon Burks (foot) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Hours after head coach Dan Quinn said he was “optimistic” that Burks would play in Week 10 against the Giants, the Commanders listed him as an estimated DNP for Monday. While they didn’t formally practice, the fact that the team is saying he wouldn’t have gotten on the field today isn’t an encouraging sign for a player who missed all of last week’s practices as well. The good news is there are still more practices to go, meaning Burks could still be upgraded before Thursday night’s game. We’ll see if his status changes on Tuesday when the Commanders take the practice field for the first time on the short week.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Jake Ferguson (knee) will likely be out “multiple weeks” after going down in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson exited Sunday’s game against the Colts after taking a nasty hit to his knee. While he was able to walk off under his own power and was later ruled “questionable” to return, the 27-year-old vet never got back into the game. Ferguson has caught just 19 passes for 136 yards and four touchdowns this season, with his best game coming in Week 2 (4-43-2) against the Commanders. Brevyn Spann-Ford, a 2024 UDFA, will likely take over in Ferguson’s absence but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 at this point.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.
item.description:
Jordan Davis

While the rest of the league waits to make moves ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, the Jaguars have spent Monday wheeling and dealing to improve the defensive side of the ball. Davis is the latest to join the Jaguars, who also acquired S Jessie Bates and DT Davon Godchaux in hopes of shoring up their top-10 defense. Davis signed a three-year, $78 million contract extension with the Eagles earlier this offseason and has been a staple along their defensive line since being drafted 13th overall by them in 2022. Davis has totaled 31 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and two TFLs this season and posted a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Cardinals signed QB Joey Aguilar off the Jaguars’ practice squad.
item.description:
Joey Aguilar ARI Quarterback

With Gardner Minshew looking at a lengthy absence, Aguilar figures to be Arizona’s No. 2 behind Carson Beck for the time being. Aguilar completed 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown in preseason action with the Jaguars after being signed as a UDFA after this year’s draft.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
item.description:
Gardner Minshew ARI Quarterback

Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cardinals WR Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks, ending his season.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

It’s a tough and unexpected loss for the Cardinals, and Wilson, who was not reported to have suffered any injury after the game. Wilson was on track for another solid season after breaking out for 76-1,006-7 last season. He was averaging a solid 9.8 targets per game this season, and never saw fewer than seven targets in any game. Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension earlier this offseason and will hopefully recover in time to be back for the start of training camp next season. Now without the top three receivers they opened the season with, the Cardinals will likely lean on the trio of Harrison Wallace III, Reggie Virgil, and Simi Fehoko for the remainder of the season.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and didn’t rule out a stint on injured reserve.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

LaFleur confirmed previous reports that Jacobs will undergo surgery, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing more than the three-week “maximum” that was reported. LaFleur not only said a stint on injured reserve was possible, but also noted that Jacobs playing through the injury was never an option, saying he “had no grip strength.” We don’t yet know when Jacobs will undergo his surgery, but LaFleur did confirm that it will be some time this week. With Jacobs now sidelined for the foreseeable future, Green Bay will look to MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson to lead the backfield heading into Week 10 against the Vikings.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said C Erik McCoy is expected to miss some time with a bicep injury
item.description:
Erik McCoy NO Center

McCoy missed 10 games last season due to a torn biceps. It doesn’t sound like his injury is nearly as severe this time around, as Moore said he believes McCoy will avoid surgery. That said, it sounds like the veteran center could be headed for injured reserve with hopes he will return at some point in the season. McCoy has started all eight games he has appeared in this season, earning a PFF grade of 73.2 while allowing just five pressures on 352 pass-blocking downs. He was replaced by Will Sherman in Week 9’s win over the Browns, with Sherman being the favorite to take over in the weeks ahead while McCoy is sidelined.

Source: Ross Jackson

item.title: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he expects Jacoby Brissett to start in Week 10 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett BAL Quarterback

The Ravens wasted little time in trading for Brissett after he lost his starting job with the Cardinals. The 33-year-old journeyman is familiar with Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork and was acquired in part because the team believed he could quickly become the starter. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in his eight games with the Cardinals this season, and will now look to save the Ravens’ season after they fell to 4-5 last week. With Lamar Jackson (finger) hoping to come back in the next six to nine weeks, if Baltimore can string together a few wins, it’s possible he will be back in time for the playoffs should they make the postseason. Brissett being under center should also provide some stability to Zay Flowers’ and Derrick Henry’s fantasy stocks after a rough few weeks sans Lamar.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said RB Tyler Goodson (knee) is expected to miss some time.
item.description:
Tyler Goodson DAL Running Back

Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys’ RB2 this season, and rushed 12 times for 77 yards in Week 9’s win over the Colts. He played through the knee injury he suffered in the second quarter. The fact that he played through the injury suggests this isn’t anything too serious, but it’s not uncommon to see players be sidelined in the following weeks once the adrenaline has worn off and the game is over. We’ll likely get a clearer timeline for his return in the coming days, but for now, it looks like Israel Abanikanda and/or Jashaun Corbin will be promoted from the practice squad, with Javonte Williams being the only healthy back on Dallas’ roster.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Speaking Monday, Browns head coach Todd Monken declined to name a starting QB for Week 10’s game against the Texans.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier in the day that Deshaun Watson was expected to return as the starter, but Monken didn’t rush to name a starter when questioned on Monday. Monken praised Shedeur Sanders for his performance in Sunday’s start against the Saints, but said he hasn’t really “thought through” who will start in Week 10 against the Texans. It’s hard to imagine Monken handing the job over to Sanders after a start that was mostly forgettable until the final five minutes of regulation, even if Watson hasn’t been overly impressive this season. We would still expect Watson to get the nod against Houston, but Sanders’ late-game performance won’t do anything to quiet those looking/hoping for a change.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Jets traded S Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
item.description:
Andre Cisco DET Safety

Cisco has started four of the nine games he has appeared in for the Jets this season, racking up 23 tackles, one sack, and one pass breakup while also forcing a fumble. The sixth-year safety has 59 games of starting experience and should provide some help on the back end to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards this season. He has graded out well as a run stopper in each of his last two seasons, per PFF, and can also line up in the slot when needed.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jaguars acquired DT Davon Godchaux from the Saints in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
item.description:
Davon Godchaux

Godchaux becomes the second defensive player the Jaguars have added ahead of the deadline. Early Monday morning, they went out and acquired safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons to improve their secondary, and now they’ve added Godchaux to bolster a defensive line that has been dealt a few injuries in recent weeks. Godchaux, like Bates, is also on an expiring contract, but should provide a small upgrade to what is already a top-10 defense. The 31-year-old lineman has totaled 15 tackles and one TFL this season while appearing on 163 snaps, with most of his contributions coming in run defense.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is considered “day-to-day.”
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

This news comes less than 24 hours after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that an MRI “did not reveal a major injury” to Mahomes, who was able to finish out the game in Sunday’s win over the Jets. Reid said Mahomes is dealing with some soreness that he will have to rehab a bit, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing any time. Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets and will be on the QB1 radar next week against the Falcons.

Source: Sam McDowell

item.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team expects Drew Lock (oblique) to start in Week 10 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Speaking on Monday, Macdonald said that tests on Lock’s oblique injury were “good” and that they believe his injury is something the team can manage. Lock has been solid in three games for the Seahawks this season, throwing for 597-5-0 while completing 71.1 percent of his passes. He draws a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Raiders and could be on the radar as a mid to low-end QB2 that may have some stream appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 10 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Macdonald said Darnold will need at least one more week to recover from the quad injury that sidelined him in Week 9. While Drew Lock (oblique) is dealing with his own injury, Macdonald said he believes the team can manage it and expects him to start next week against the Raiders. The Seahawks will have their bye in Week 11, so hopefully three straight weeks off will give him enough time to recover before Week 12’s game against the 49ers.

Source: John Boyle

item.title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team plans to bring A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) to Germany ahead of Week 10’s game against the Lions.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

This doesn’t mean Brown will suit up against the Lions, but it is an indicator that the team thinks he has a chance to play if he can have a good week of practice. Brown has missed the Patriots’ last two games after a knee injury flared up following Week 7’s game against the Bears. He did not get on the practice field at all last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an improvement for the 29-year-old receiver. In three games this season, Brown has caught just 9-of-20 targets for 101 scoreless yards. That said, if he’s healthy enough to play in Week 10, he could be primed for a breakout against a lowly Lions secondary.

Source: Doug Kyed

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will be “full go” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Harbaugh said Skattebo was “very close” to playing in Week 9 against the Eagles, but they opted to sideline him, focusing on the second game they would play four days later. With the Giants set to face the Commanders on Thursday, Skattebo should be well rested and ready to play in his first game since Week 7, when he first suffered his injury. Skattebo totaled 71 scoreless yards on 15 touches in Week 5 against the Commanders and will be in the RB2 mix upon returning this week.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Panthers “have received calls” on DT Derrick Brown’s availability via trade.
item.description:
Derrick Brown CAR Defensive Tackle

The Panthers have said that they are “not actively looking to move Brown,” but Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported last week that they have considered it. One of the premier DTs in the league, Brown could fetch a decent pick haul if the Panthers were willing to move him. With the NFL trade deadline set to pass on Tuesday, we will soon know the fate of several players who are rumored to be on the move, but it sounds like it will take a lot for the Panthers to give up Brown.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
James Cook BUF Running Back

Cook struggled to 2.7 yards per carry through the first three quarters but made his mark felt in the final frame, adding his his lone rushing score in the fourth quarter to bring his season total to eight. The yardage total also pushed him over 5,000 career rush yards, doing so in the same game as Josh Allen to become the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. Cook has now scored in seven straight games as he continues his bid for one of the top fantasy running backs in the league. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets.

item.title: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Kyle Hamilton “looks fairly good” after suffering a hip injury in Week 9’s loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Kyle Hamilton BAL Safety

Hamilton exited Thursday’s game and did not return to the field. Despite the scare, it doesn’t sound like Hamilton is at risk of missing much, if any, time. The two-time All-Pro has totaled 60 tackles, nine TFLs, and one interception this season while also breaking up five passes.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving’s touches could decrease in the second half of the season to preserve his health.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

As Bucs beat writer Greg Auman points out, Irving is on pace for 315 carries this season, which would have been the second most in the league last year. Irving has not missed a game yet this season, but after injuries limited him to 10 games in 2025, it’s not surprising to learn Bowles may want to dial things back a bit. The efficient play of Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks has also earned him an expanded look, and it should instill a bit of confidence in OC Zac Robinson when asking him to spell Irving in certain situations. With the Bucs now entering their bye week, we will get our first look at how the team plans to deploy its backfield in Week 11 when they visit the Lions.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he is “optimistic” that Treylon Burks (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks sat out in Sunday’s loss to the Rams due to a foot injury that kept him off the practice field all week. Quinn’s optimism suggests he will at least be listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report and will get on the field in some capacity on Tuesday and Wednesday. Burks has been a solid downfield threat for the Commanders this year, catching 12 passes for 233 yards and two touchdowns. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him outside of deeper leagues, where he could be a viable desperation play as a WR4. In addition to Burks, Quinn also said he was hopeful CB Amik Robertson (ankle) would be ready to play on Thursday against the Giants.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Panthers “have received calls” on DT Derrick Brown’s availability via trade.
item.description:
Derrick Brown CAR Defensive Tackle

The Panthers have said that they are “not actively looking to move Brown,” but it Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported last week that they have considered it. One of the premier DTs in the league, Brown could fetch a decent pick haul if the Panthers were willing to move him. With the NFL trade deadline set to pass on Tuesday, we will soon know the fate of several players who are rumored to be on the move, but it sounds like it will take a lot for the Panthers to give up Brown.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Browns “plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs. the Texans.”
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

This shouldn’t surprise anyone after Shedeur Sanders failed to make the most of his spot start in Week 9 against the Saints. Sanders and the Browns’ offense stalled through the first three quarters of Sunday’s game before a late 64-yard touchdown pass to KC Concepcion gave the Browns their first touchdown of the day. An impressive catch-and-run score by Harold Fannin in overtime gave Sanders his second touchdown pass on the day, but the 39-yard score came on a pass, in which Fannin generated 37 yards after the catch. Watson has struggled mightily at times this season, but Sanders didn’t do enough to unseat him in what was a plus matchup against a bad defense. Now out of concussion protocol, Watson will suit up in a “revenge game” against his former team next week, where he will profile as a low-end QB2.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said J.J. McCarthy (hip) looks “like he’s going to play” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

Harbaugh said McCarthy is “doing well” after briefly being knocked out of Sunday’s game against the Eagles with a hip injury. McCarthy was in visible pain on the sideline at times, but was able to finish the game. We’ll see how things shape up over the week as the Giants prepare for a short turnaround ahead of Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. If he’s healthy enough, McCarthy will get the start against a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily at times against the pass this season.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Speaking after Week 9’s win over the Commanders, Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) will likely be out a “couple [of] weeks.”
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson was set to return in Week 9 against the Commanders prior to suffering a pulled hamstring. According to McVay, the second-year tight end was going to be a “big part” of the Rams’ offensive game plan against the Commanders, which should be good news to fantasy managers still holding out hope for a return. Based on McVay’s comments, we can safely assume Ferguson won’t be playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, and then the Rams head into their bye. If all goes well in his recovery, it’s possible he could return on a short week in Week 12 to play against the Packers, but we likely won’t have more clarity on that until after their bye. For now, Ferguson remains a worthwhile stash in leagues where you can afford to do so, but it’s hard to say with any confidence when we should expect him to be back on the field.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley was involved in an “unfortunate” incident at Nashville airport.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

Saleh didn’t get into the details of the matter, instead opting to say it was a “very minor miscommunication” that is “now in the hands of law enforcement.” Ridley, 31, has caught 6-of-12 targets for 91 scoreless yards this season and could find himself on the move ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. That said, he’s far from the difference-making player he was early in his career and is fourth among Titans receivers in routes run (124) this season.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jets DE Will McDonald has requested a trade.
item.description:
Will McDonald NYJ Defensive End

McDonald has been lightly used this season by the Jets. The former first-rounder has appeared in all nine games this season, totaling three sacks and 15 tackles while appearing on just 278 defensive snaps, per PFF. According to Rapoport, the Jets have not engaged in trade talks for McDonald despite receiving calls, and “they have no plans to.” With a 2-7 record, the Jets should be sellers, but have maintained for over a week that they would prefer not to move many players, if any.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Falcons traded S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
item.description:
Jessie Bates

The Jaguars also sent a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons in exchange for Bates, who is in the final year of his contract. Bates provides an immediate upgrade to a defensive unit that already ranks top-10 in points and yards allowed per game but has been more susceptible to being hurt through the air. Bates is a three-time Second-Team All-Pro and among the top safeties in the league. It stands to reason that the Jaguars will look to extend him at some point next offseason, but for now, he will join a 6-2 team that is clearly willing to go all in on what could be a deep run in the postseason.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Chris Godwin caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Chris Godwin TB Wide Receiver

The only positive to take from this is every Tampa Bay receiver who caught a pass clobbered their production from the week before. Godwin did have a 12-yard rush, but it’s another clunker for the wideout in a year where Godwin has yet to reach 50 yards. It’s a mistake to bet that mark will be reached in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Cade Otton TB Tight End

Otton was targeted a couple of times in the end zone, but Baker Mayfield wasn’t able to connect with the tight end on either attempt. The 25 yards are his most since Week 5, but it’s still a middling — at best — effort for the 27-year-old. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere in Week 11 against the Lions after Tampa Bay’s bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

It was Egbuka’s first game since Week 6 because of his foot injury, and it was pretty similar to his previous efforts in 2026. He was able to get lose for a 21-yard catch from the arm of Baker Mayfield, but once again, he was unable to eclipse 50 yards; a mark he hasn’t bested since Week 3. Egbuka is a high-floor, low-ceiling WR3 going forward, and the next chance will come after a bye in Week 11 against the Lions.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tez Johnson caught 2-of-5 targets for 76 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Tez Johnson TB Wide Receiver

Johnson’s 58-yard connection with Baker Mayfield set up a rushing score from Bucky Irving. He also had two big drops on third down that would have kept drives going for the Bucs, and on the first he was seen taking out his frustration on his helmet. Johnson ended up leading the Bucs in receiving yards and tied for the lead in targets, but that’s not quite the compliment it should be. Johnson and Tampa Bay get a bye before a showdown with the Lions in Week 11.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kalif Raymond caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Kalif Raymond CHI Wide Receiver

Raymond had a quiet day, but made a huge 13-yard catch on the final drive that ended with a Cairo Santos’ game-winning field goal. Luther Burden exited the game with a head injury late, and if Burden can’t go in Week 11 after the bye, Raymond will be an intriguing dart throw for that contest. If Burden can go, he’s tough to trust in redraft formats.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-7 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

Odunze couldn’t quite haul in a touchdown throw from Caleb Williams on the first drive of the game, but on the next play, he was able to reach the end zone for his first touchdown of the 2026 season. He could have had another, but a perfect throw from Williams bounced off his hands with nothing but green grass in front of him. Still, it’s another competent game for the former first-round pick, and he’s reached 60 yards in each of his last three contests. Odunze belongs in the WR3 range for Week 11 against the Saints after a Week 10 bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: D’Andre Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift didn’t catch his lone target in a bust of a contest for the veteran tailback. He had a long gain of just six yards, and was nearly outrun by Salvon Ahmed who finished with 25 yards on the ground. Yes, that Salvon Ahmed. It’s a disappointing — but not terribly surprising — follow-up to the three touchdowns he had Monday night in Week 8, but this is what Swift has done throughout his career. He’ll be a RB2 for Week 11 against the Saints after the Bears’ enjoy their bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kenny Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 60 yards.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Most of Gainwell’s yardage came on a 44-yard busted coverage that set up the Bucs’ first score of the game. He found little room in the run game after gashing the Falcons for 140 yards. The 1A/1B talk that head coach Todd Bowles mentioned with Gainwell and Bucky Irving never really came to fruition, as Irving was much more effective with 97 yards on the ground and a pair of scores. Gainwell remains a RB3 going forward, with his next chance to contribute coming in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Luther Burden left Week 9’s game against the Buccaneers with an apparent injury. He finished with 7 catches for 97 yards and a touchdown before exiting.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

Burden fumbled and set up Tampa Bay’s tying score in the fourth quarter after a shot that could have easily been a helmet-to-helmet penalty. The 22-year-old did most of his damage on a 58-yard score that gave Chicago a 14-0 lead. Burden will assuredly undergo concussion testing, but it’s worth noting the Bears don’t play again until Week 11 against the Lions because of a bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Bucky Irving rushed 20 times for 97 yards and two scores in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding four catches for 28 yards.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

Irving was held in check for the first three quarters outside of a short rushing touchdown, but broke several tackles to open the fourth quarter on a 25-yard gain. He scored again in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 24-24 and now has six rushing scores in 2026. It wasn’t quite the monster effort he produced against the Falcons (27/170/1) the week prior, but still a very strong fantasy day for the 24-year-old tailback. Irving should be considered as an RB1 against the Lions in Week 11 after a bye.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Baker Mayfield completed 18-of-32 passes for 243 yards with two interceptions in the Buccaneers’ 27-24, Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Well, it was infinitely better than last week. Mayfield made two long connections; a 44-yarder to Kenny Gainwell to set up a field goal, and a beautiful 58-yard lob to Tez Johnson that was followed by Bucky Irving score. Unfortunately, his only scoring pass went the wrong way as it was a 67-yard pick-six from Jaylon Johnson that made it a two-score game. He did at least run in a two-point conversion that tied the game at 24-24, but the Bears were able to pull out the win on a last-second field goal. Mayfield also looked to be uncomfortable on the sidelines, as the Bears generated pressure throughout the contest. The Bucs get a needed bye next week, and Mayfield will be a QB2 for Week 11 against the Lions.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes Josh Downs “is finding that he is best suited to play the role he has always played.”
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

The Colts have given Downs the opportunity to expand his offensive involvement this year, but he has struggled to capitalize on it without Alec Piece (heel) on the field to keep defenses honest. Downs reportedly asked for a trade roughly two weeks ago, and per Holder, the relationship between Downs and the Colts isn’t “the best” right now. If they can’t get adequate trade value, they may choose to keep him, while also using the lack of a substantial offer as a counterpoint to his recent disgruntlement. Stay tuned.

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he did not consider benching Gardner Minshew for Carson Beck at any point in Arizona’s Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

We don’t believe him. But it really doesn’t matter because Beck will get his chance at some point in the coming weeks. The Cardinals’ rookie looked good in the preseason Hall of Fame game, though it is unclear whether he can do enough to warrant QB2 treatment as a pure pocket passer. The Cardinals’ schedule softens after matchups against the Rams and Chiefs over the next two weeks. Beck should have a chance to play in Week 12 against the Commanders, if not sooner.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Audric Estime rushed 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Audric Estime NO Running Back

Estime was waived by the Browns on Monday. The Saints claimed him on Tuesday and he was their starting back by Sunday. Life comes at you fast. Kellen Moore made it a point to get Estime going early with three carries for him on their first three plays of the game. He gashed the Browns 32 yards on those three attempts alone. He would later punch in a goal line touchdown to give the Saints the lead in the fourth quarter. Estime will be the Saints’ lead runner until Travis Etienne is activated from injured reserve. That could happen as soon as Week 10, so fantasy managers shouldn’t count on another usable week from Estime anytime soon.

item.title: Brandin Cooks caught both of his targets for 25 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
item.description:
Brandin Cooks SF Wide Receiver

Cooks ran about 30 percent of the team’s routes and was fourth in targets among Niners pass catchers. With Jordan Watkins and Demarcus Robinson in the fold, Cooks should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 10.

item.title: Andre Szmyt converted 3-of-3 field goal attempts in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
item.description:
Andre Szmyt CLE Kicker

Szmyt nailed his third attempt, a 51-yarder to send the game into overtime. He has attempted at least three field goals in three of his past four games. Both of his misses, however, have come in the past month. Cleveland’s hit-or-miss offense makes Szmyt a risky fantasy option, but he’s hanging around the top-12 halfway through the 2026 season.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey had 18 rushes for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey didn’t have much trouble against a Vegas run defense that has been one of the league’s worst over the past month. His rushing score was his ninth of the season, while his receiving score was his first of 2026. CMC logged 28 routes on the day while Kaelon Black had just five routes and did not see a target from Brock Purdy. McCaffrey, with at least 15 carries in five games this year, has a spectacular Week 10 matchup against a miserable Dallas defense.

item.title: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns, adding three catches for 17 yards.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

The Saints added Audric Estime via waivers on Monday and he went on to lead the team in carries today. He saw 15 rushes plus one target. Estime also found the end zone after Kamara was tackled at the two-yard line. Kamara was the team’s primary back on passing downs, but his role between the tackles remained incredibly limited. With Travis Etienne potentially returning next week, his role could take another hit in Week 10. He remains a low-upside RB4 for his upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

item.title: Tyler Shough completed 21-of-35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ 23-22, Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Tyler Shough NO Quarterback

Shough got off to a dreadfully slow start, throwing for a measly 156 scoreless yards over the first three quarters. The Browns weren’t pushing the Saints to play fast or pass often, resulting in a noticeable lack of volume for Shough. A 64-yard touchdown for the Browns in the middle of the fourth quarter finally forced the Saints to pick up the pace. Shough responded with a 55-yard touchdown drive two series later, though Audric Estime found the end zone on the ground. Shough eventually closed out the game with a 15-yard touchdown strike to Juwan Johnson in overtime. Shough’s fantasy output is tied directly to his passing volume. He’ll remain at the top of the QB2 ranks as long as his defense keeps giving up points, which should happen versus the Panthers in Week 10.

item.title: Demarcus Robinson caught 3-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

Robinson was back from his ankle injury, though the CBS broadcast mentioned Robinson was only about 50 percent back from the ankle issue. He logged a pass route on 21 of the team’s 36 drop backs and was tied for second in targets. Jordan Watkins — who had a 37-yard score against Vegas — appears to be the Niners’ No. 1 wideout for now (with Mike Evans sidelined). Robinson can be rostered in deeper leagues.

item.title: Kaelon Black had 11 rushes for 70 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Christian McCaffrey, meanwhile, had 18 rushes on the day and scored two touchdowns. Black had just five pass routes against the Raiders while CMC ran 28 routes. Black’s 70 rushing yards marks a season high and shows he can be a fantasy factor when the Niners have game script in their favor. It didn’t help that he faced an abysmal Raiders front seven. Black should have some flex viability in deeper leagues next week against the Cowboys.

item.title: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-37 passes for 279 yards with two touchdowns and four interceptions in the Bears’ 27-24, Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

An absolutely bizarre football game. Williams was brilliant on the first two drives with two touchdowns. After that, things got weird at best and disastrous at worst. He threw interceptions on back-to-back throws in the second quarter, and threw two more picks for his first career four-INT game. Kudos to the Bucs for generating the pressure necessary to create those picks — this is back-to-back four interception games for the Tampa Bay defense — but three of the four interceptions were egregious throws. He was able to get the job done at the end of the night, hitting Colston Loveland on a blown coverage for a 38-yard gain that set up the game-winning field goal. He’ll get a week to review the tape on bye before taking on the Saints in Week 11.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes the Colts could receive “an 11th-hour offer” for Jonathan Taylor that convinces Indianapolis to trade him.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Holder’s sources are currently telling him that there is “not a strong indication” that the Colts will be busy making deals at Tuesday’s trade deadline, but he adds that “you can’t rule this out with Taylor.” The Colts already received an offer including a second- and a fifth-round pick. Holder wonders aloud whether a second- and a third-round pick could be enough for Indianapolis to trade him away. Reading between the lines, that could be the Colts leaking an asking price to him. We’ll find out for sure in less than 48 hours. Stay tuned.

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

Mayer was second on the team in pass routes behind Brock Bowers. He nearly had not one, but two touchdown catches on the day. Mayer had the ball knocked out of his hand as he reached for the goal line in the first half, and was called for pass interference on a short touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. It was a tough luck day for the Raiders’ TE2. With 15 receptions over the past three games coming into Week 9, Mayer is usable in deeper formats going forward. He gets the Seahawks in Week 10.

item.title: Chris Olave caught 7-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

It was business as usual for Olave, who has seen at least 10 targets in 6-of-8 games this year. He earned an astounding 38 percent target share today, and his 229 air yards are the second-most of the week, pending the two remaining games. The return of No. 8 overall pick Jorydn Tyson had no impact on his role, though Tyson was limited to 16 routes in his NFL debut. Tyson should see more work next week, but that will primarily come at the expense of Devaughn Vele. Olave will remain in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Panthers in Week 10.

item.title: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-32 attempts for 216 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

The statuesque Cousins was under duress from start to finish, often falling back as he threw the ball into tight windows. That led to three picks, which should have been four or five picks if 49ers defenders had been a little more sure handed. As usual, Cousins targeted Brock Bowers relentlessly, once again connecting with the superstar tight end for a touchdown. He nearly threw a second touchdown to Bowers in the second half. Cousins also had a touchdown to Michael Mayer called back on an offensive pass interference penalty. This was only Cousins’ second game of the year with less than two TD passes. Cousins will be a superflex option in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

item.title: Juwan Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson split reps with Noah Fant and Oscar Delp once again. He had one catch headed into overtime but made the most of the extra drive with a game-winning touchdown grab. It was his first touchdown since Week 3. This was also his first multi-catch game since Week 5. With Jordyn Tyson set to take on a larger role in the coming weeks, Johnson’s days as a high-end TE2 appear to be over. Fantasy managers can do better off the waiver wire in Week 10.

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending ankle fracture.
item.description:
Gracen Halton SF Defensive Lineman

The fourth-round rookie finishes the year with 10 tackles, eight quarterback pressures and two sacks. Shanahan also told reporters that starting cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) picked up injuries in today’s game against the Raiders. The defense has been hit hard by injuries this season. Hopefully, the cornerbacks are back before long.

Source: Cam Inman

item.title: Jordyn Tyson caught 4-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Tyson was activated from injured reserve over the weekend and made his NFL debut today. He got off to a nightmare start by fumbling his first career reception inside the five-yard line. The Saints didn’t go away from him after the rookie mistake and rotated him onto the field rather sporadically for the rest of the game. He was deployed as the team’s WR3, running 16 routes compared to 44 for Devaughn Vele. Those two numbers should converge in the coming weeks, but it might take some time for Tyson to overtake Vele as the team’s WR2. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for Week 10 against the Panthers.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo’s seven targets tied Van Jefferson for the team high in this one. Okonkwo hauled in a 15-yard reception on the Commanders’ opening drive, and on the final play of the game, he caught a 16-yard pass and then tossed it to Rachaad White in hopes of keeping the play alive after time had already expired. Okonkwo has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and is seeing enough work in the passing game to be on the streaming radar for Week 10’s game against the Giants.

item.title: Kimani Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding one reception for six yards.
item.description:
Kimani Vidal LAC Running Back

Vidal was regularly involved early on, but logged just two offensive touches after being on the receiving end of a facemask penalty committed by a Texans defender on the Chargers’ fourth drive. Vidal did, however, remain involved on special teams all game long. He is off the FLEX radar against the Ravens next week.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding three receptions for 34 yards.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell regularly rotated in and out as a member of the Chargers’ three-player backfield rotation, though he and Omarion Hampton remained far more involved than Kimani Vidal did in the second half. He looks spry as a rusher and receiver, ripping off double-digit gains in both facets of the game. Unfortunately, Mitchell’s biggest contribution was a fumble in enemy territory, which the Texans recovered inside the red zone. Mitchell is just a floor-based FLEX against his former Ravens team next week.

item.title: Omarion Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that Omarion Hampton would get more touches. Surprise. The Chargers continued their three-player backfield rotation for much of the day, though Kimani Vidal was somewhat phased out in the second half. That said, Hampton at least totaled double-digit rushing attempts for the first time since Week 5. He clearly looked like the most powerful, explosive Chargers running back on a 32-yard run late in the game, jump-cutting his way into an open hole before exploding down the right side of the field. Hampton is a FLEX option against the Ravens in Week 10.

item.title: DJ Uiagalelei completed 2-of-7 targets for 24 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
DJ Uiagalelei LAC Quarterback

Uiagalelei entered the game in the fourth quarter after Justin Herbert suffered what coach Jim Harbaugh said could be a fracture in his left, non-throwing hand. Uiagalelei linked up with Derius Davis for a 15-yard score late in the game. Both players did a good job on the scoring sequence. Uiagalelei will be a QB3 against the Ravens if he gets the start next week.

item.title: Tre’ Harris caught 3-of-7 targets for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

Being this inefficient ain’t easy. Trainers examined Harris’ lower left leg after an eighth-drive incompletion in which Harris twisted as he unsuccessfully tried to high-point a pass and came down hard on his feet. Harris does not need to be in fantasy football lineups against the Ravens next week.

item.title: Jordan Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
item.description:
Jordan Watkins SF Wide Receiver

Watkins’ big day was capped off by a second half 37-yard touchdown grab on a perfectly placed ball from Brock Purdy. Watkins, who had 56 yards on three receptions in Week 7, functioned as the Niners’ top wideout with Mike Evans (Achilles) out. Watkins led the Niners in pass routes against a lousy Raiders secondary. He’ll be in play as a WR3 option in Week 10 against the Cowboys if Evans remains sidelined.

item.title: Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

Justin Herbert gave Gadsden a chance to get going downfield early on, but the pass clanged off his hands. The incompletion may ultimately have been erased by a penalty. Herbert looked his way again later, on the Chargers’ late two-point conversion attempt, but it failed. Charlie Kolar, meanwhile, caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and rushed once for three yards. Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats.

item.title: George Kittle caught 4-of-7 targets for 58 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

It was a fairly low volume day for Brock Purdy and the Niners passing offense. The team had 25 pass attempts to 34 designed rushes against a miserable Vegas defense. Kittle ran a route on 28 of the team’s 32 drop backs and led the Niners with seven targets. His biggest play came on a patented catch and run through the Vegas secondary — one of a few long YAC plays for the San Francisco offense. Kittle should remain in all lineups next week against a porous Dallas coverage unit.

item.title: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-4 targets for 58 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding one rush for five yards.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

If you didn’t start Johnston, we can’t blame you. It’s been a rough go. Johnston deserves credit for his long score. He caught a pass on a slant route and took off downfield via a post pattern, churning his legs through a shoestring tackle attempt. It’s the type of play we expected Johnston to be featured on in OC Mike McDaniel’s offense, rather than the deep routes he is frequently stuck running. Johnston also earned an end zone target, but was unable to secure it. With Justin Herbert (left hand) ailing, Johnston is tough to trust as a FLEX against the Ravens next week.

item.title: Kaleb Johnson rushed 14 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Kaleb Johnson GB Running Back

An early injury to Josh Jacobs (finger) opened the door for Johnson to have a career day. The former third-round pick rushed for a career-high 68 yards in this one while leading the Packers in carries and managed to find the end zone on a two-yard touchdown in the second quarter. In addition to Jacobs leaving the game early, Johnson also benefited from MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive. Half of his rushing production came on a 34-yard run, and fantasy managers should exercise caution before adding him off of waivers this week. The Packers have already said that they are going to see if Jacobs can play through his fractured finger, and it’s possible Lloyd will be active next week after entering this weekend carrying a questionable tag. If both Jacobs and Lloyd are sidelined, Johnson could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues as a boom-or-bust RB3 against the Vikings.

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) did not play in Week 9 against the Texans.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups. The Chargers kept that info under wraps until their first drive was underway, following an opening-drive touchdown by the Texans. We aren’t exactly sure how the Chargers were allowed to do this, but they did it, and fantasy managers who started him are stuck with 0.0 points in the box score. If he can face the Ravens next week, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

item.title: Woody Marks rushed 18 times for 70 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for four yards.
item.description:
Woody Marks HOU Running Back

Marks was able to earn four targets in this one, but he caught only one of them. He was heavily involved as a rusher, regularly churning out short-to-intermediate ground gains, but without steady receiving production, he is stuck in the low-end RB2 tier with touchdown-dependent upside. He will qualify as such next week against the Browns if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

item.title: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

Schultz’s box score is a tad inflated by two throwaway targets. CJ Stroud aimed passes Schultz his way while pressured, in order to avoid intentional grounding penalties. Schultz did make a great toe-tapping catch along the right sideline on the Texans’ seventh drive, and later hauled in a 28-yard pass downfield against busted coverage. Schultz is a borderline TE1/2 against the Browns next week.

item.title: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 29 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Xavier Hutchinson HOU Wide Receiver

The Texans’ run-blocking specialist isn’t going anywhere. He capped off the Texans’ opening drive with an 18-yard touchdown on third down, and came up clutch with a tough catch to pick up a first down on the ensuing drive. He later let a pass go off his fingertips 38 yards downfield, near the Texans’ 25-yard line. Had he caught it and landed on his feet, he probably could have scored. He had the secondary beat. Hutchinson cannot be trusted to return FLEX value against the Browns.

item.title: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry was playing through a foot injury in this one, but still ended up leading all Patriots tight ends in routes run (22). Prior to his injury-shortened outing in Week 8, Henry was riding a four-game streak of double-digit PPR performances, but he wasn’t able to get there this week. Hopefully, he didn’t suffer any setbacks this week and will be a viable streaming option in what could be a plus matchup next week against the Lions.

item.title: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Tucker occupied his usual role as the team’s de facto No. 1 wideout, almost connecting with Kirk Cousins in the second half for what likely would have been a long touchdown. Tucker was tied for the team lead in targets with Brock Bowers. His air yards domination gives Tucker a fairly high weekly ceiling in a Vegas offense usually chasing points in the second half. Tucker will be an iffy option next week against Seattle.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patrick Mahomes’ (elbow) MRI “did not reveal a major injury.”
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Rapoport adds that Mahomes’ “elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling.” Without getting too deep into the weeds, there are a few things to note. First off, Rapoport sometimes reports injury news optimistically. It would have been nice to see him actually report a “minor” injury, rather than not “major.” Secondly, “strain” typically refers to muscles and tendons, while “sprain” is often used for ligaments. Using both is a tad confusing. That said, Rapoport’s follow-up statement suggests Mahomes may have a chance to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Updates will be provided as soon as news breaks. Stay tuned.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

item.title: DeMario Douglas caught 5-of-9 targets for 102 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
DeMario Douglas NE Wide Receiver

The Patriots trailed throughout this one, which resulted in Drake Maye airing it out a season-high 38 times. The nine targets Douglas saw in this one also set a new season-high for the 25-year-old receiver, who reeled in two passes for 30-plus yards. Douglas has had a productive few games as of late, topping 60 receiving yards in four of his last five outings while also finding the end zone four times. He’ll be in the WR4/Flex range in Week 10 in what could be a high-scoring game against the Lions in Munich.

item.title: Corey Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Corey Kiner NE Running Back

The Patriots lost Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) late in this one, but it’s still worth noting that nearly all of Kiner’s production came when the backups were on the field. Kiner punched in a nine-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter with the game well out of reach, and broke off a 20-yard run on the second-to-last play in regulation. While it’s possible Kiner finds himself in a lead role when the Patriots take on the Lions next week, fantasy managers will want to temper expectations for Week 10 if either Stevenson (knee) or TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is active.

item.title: Marvin Harrison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Harrison was fairly quiet today, though CJ Stroud picked on Chargers CB Duke Shelley on the Texans’ seventh drive, and Harrison did manage to get in on the fun, beating Shelley for a 15-yard, tip-toe catch along the right sideline. Harrison remains a boom-bust FLEX against the Browns next week, as he continues adjusting to the Texans’ offensive scheme.

item.title: Tank Dell caught 4-of-9 targets for 105 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

The Texans seemed fairly comfortable using Dell in this one, getting him going with a screen pass on the opening drive. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard touchdown via a go route, in which he simply ran past his coverage defender down the right sideline. CJ Stroud hit Dell in stride and he continued on down the field and into the end zone. Dell managed to earn an end zone target on the Texans’ 11th drive, but was unable to secure it. Dell is officially on the WR3/FLEX radar for Week 10 against the Browns.

item.title: Mack Hollins caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Playing in his first game since Week 4, Hollins ran a season-high 34 routes and tied Eli Rairdon for the second-most targets among Patriots pass-catchers on the day. Hollins found the end zone on a 22-yard score in the third quarter with the Packers already well ahead, which gave Hollins his first touchdown of the season. Hollins has been targeted five or more times in three of his five games this season and could be a deep league streaming option next week against the Lions if A.J. Brown (knee) misses next week.

item.title: Nico Collins caught 4-of-4 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins delivered a 19-yard catch-and-run on the Texans’ opening drive. He played particularly well running curl route today. His one-handed touchdown has to be seen to be believed. He and his coverage defender went vertical in the end zone and Collins somehow underhanded the pass around the other player’s body, briefly pinning it to the defender’s torso to secure it. Collins is a locked-in WR1 against the Browns next week.

item.title: Devaughn Vele caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
item.description:
Devaughn Vele NO Wide Receiver

As expected, the return of Jordyn Tyson brought about the end of Vele’s time as a WR3 fantasy option. Though Vele got his normal complement of routes, Tyson out-targeted him 5-4. He also went for more yards on two extra catches. Tyson’s role is only going to grow as he gets more practice reps under his belt. Fantasy managers can thank Vele for the good times and send him to the waiver wire on this week’s run. He will be buried in the WR5/6 range for Week 10 versus the Panthers.

item.title: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception in the Texans’ 44-22, Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding two rushes for 20 yards.
item.description:
C.J. Stroud HOU Quarterback

Stroud was nonchalantly excellent today, linking up with four different pass catchers for five touchdowns. He capped off the opening drive with a 17-yard, third-down touchdown strike to Xavier Hutchinson. Tank Dell hauled in Stroud’s second touchdown in stride, beating his coverage defender and racing into the end zone for a 63-yard score. Kayshoun Boutte bagged two, including one against Chargers CB Duke Shelley, who Stroud picked on for much of the Texans’ seventh drive. He hit Nico Collins for an improbable one-handed score, in which Collins briefly pinned the football against his coverage defender’s torso to secure the catch. Stroud’s lone mistake was an off-target interception that one Chargers defender tipped to another. Stroud should remain in fantasy football lineups as a QB1 next week against the Browns.

item.title: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
item.description:
Jerry Jeudy CLE Wide Receiver

Jeudy reeled in a game-changing 30-yard pass on the Browns’ final drive of regulation. The grab eventually set up a tying field goal from Andre Szmyt. While the Browns would go on to lose in overtime, Jeudy’s catch at least gave them a shot at the win. He’s not on the fantasy radar right now, but his occasional big play should be enough to keep the Browns from trading him ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Interestingly, Kraft had a more productive day on the ground (2-8-0) in what was a quiet day for the 26-year-old tight end. His quiet day can be partly blamed on a hyper-efficient passing attack that saw Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combine for 335 of the 372 receiving yards the Packers managed on the day. The three targets Kraft saw tied a season low, and he averaged 6.7 targets per game over his last six games. He will look to bounce back next week at home against the Vikings and will profile as a low-end TE1.

item.title: Denzel Boston caught 6-of-7 targets for 98 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Like clockwork, Boston beat his man for a massive play again this week. Boston plucked a deep ball right off Kool-Aid McKinstry’s helmet and ran inside the five-yard line for a 60-yard gain early in the third quarter. It was his league-leading fourth catch of 40+ yards this year. Despite operating as a deep threat, Boston went on to lead the Browns in all receiving categories except touchdowns. Boston continues to look like a high-end boundary receiver in the mold of Tee Higgins or Mike Evans. While he’s got a long way to go to match those players, the early returns have been promising. Boston will remain a high-ceiling WR3 when he takes on the Texans next week.

item.title: AJ Barner caught 2-of-4 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding three yards and a touchdown on three carries.
item.description:
AJ Barner SEA Tight End

Barner kicked off the scoring in the second quarter with a tight end sneak from one yard out, adding a second score on the following possession on a beautiful, fingertip grab in the flat from seven yards out. Quarterback Drew Lock delivered the football late and behind the veteran tight end, the latter of whom adjusted in the face of suffocating pressure to pluck the football from the air and hold on through the ground for the touchdown. Barner remains highly unlikely to see consistent weekly volume in this Seattle offense, but fantasy managers can benefit from high variance touchdowns every so often.

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Cooper Kupp caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Backup quarterback Drew Lock attempted only 28 passes on a night their defense held the Cardinals to under 200 yards of total offense, leaving little more than scraps for Kupp, despite the absence of Rashid Shaheed. Further uncertainty persists given the multi-game injury to starting quarterback Sam Darnold and the oblique injury sustained by Lock, with the offense potentially helmed by Jalen Milroe when they face the Raiders in Week 10. Kupp remains far from the fantasy radar.

item.title: Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs exited early in the first quarter after his finger got caught in a defender’s facemask while he attempted a stiff arm. While he was never officially ruled out, Jacobs never returned to the field and was instead on the sideline in full uniform. According to Schneidman, the Packers plan to find a way for Jacobs to play through the injury, but he was unable to return in this one. Although, to be fair, he also wasn’t needed, as the Packers’ offense was in control throughout the evening. We assume Jacobs would see close to a normal workload if he is active for Week 10 against the Vikings, meaning fantasy manager can treat him as a strong RB2.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 7-of-10 targets for 51 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over he Cardinals.
item.description:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba SEA Wide Receiver

The fact that 54 yards is something to talk about says enough about the year Smith-Njigba is having, still handily leading the league in receiving despite the down performance. He remained the clear top dog through the air, receiving 10 targets on only 28 Lock pass attempts, largely confined to short area work as the Seahawks struggled to decipher the zone-heavy and two-high-heavy Arizona defense. Lock suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter that could place his Week 10 status in doubt, despite not missing an offensive snap, meaning fantasy managers of Smith-Njigba will want to monitor the situation ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders considering Sam Darnold remains unlikely to play with a multi-week injury.

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert may have suffered a left-hand fracture in the Chargers’ 22-44, Week 9 loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Justin Herbert LAC Quarterback

Last year, when Herbert injured his left, non-throwing hand, his trainers stabilized the hand, with extra padding and tape applied to his middle finger. The exact same thing happened today. Herbert fended off a pass rusher with his left hand before bracing himself with the same hand as he fell. Fortunately, he remained in the game long enough to complete a 58-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. After a trip to the blue medical tent, Herbert was on the sideline, helmet on, with his left hand and middle finger heavily taped and padded. However, he did not return. The Chargers’ pass protection remains a huge problem, allowing eight sacks on the day. Herbert told reporters post-game that he does not expect his left middle finger to be an issue going forward. We will know more once he undergoes imaging. Stay tuned.

Source: Alex Insdorf

item.title: Jadarian Price rushed nine times for 24 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 54 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price’s 13 opportunities lagged the 18 of Zach Charbonnet in what is developing into a true 60-40 split between him and the veteran, and while the 54 yards through the air were impressive, Price appears to need consistent aerial production to sustain his fantasy value moving forward while playing on the wrong side of a timeshare. Hopefully he can improve upon the modest 2.7 yards per carry he notched against the Cardinals when the Seahawks take on the sliding Raiders in Week 10.

item.title: Zach Charbonnet rushed 16 times for 77 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding nine yards on one reception.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Charbonnet served as the clear lead back against an inferior Cardinals team, handling 16 carries and two targets to the nine carries and four targets of rookie Jadarian Price. The roughly 60-40 split between the two is likely closer to what to expect for the remainder of the season now that Charbonnet has another game under his belt coming off the 2025 torn ACL. The fantasy returns could be much greater against arguably the worst defense in the league at present, with Charbonnet inching closer to weekly FLEX status ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders.

item.title: Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans.

item.title: Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. The team passed an update on Lock’s oblique injury following the game, indicating that the veteran journeyman would undergo follow-on testing but that his status for Week 10 could be in doubt.

item.title: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

item.title: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

item.title: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 54 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

The lone incompletion directed toward McBride came on the team’s final play of the game when the veteran tight end was unable to corral an end zone target that was thrown slightly behind him on fourth and goal. McBride combined with alpha wide receiver Michael Wilson to account for 15 targets on 30 Minshew pass attempts, something we’d expect to continue forward give the current state of the team. The Cardinals get another difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 10, where McBride will remain a surefire TE1 in fantasy circles.

item.title: Michael Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 60 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

The lone Gardner Minshew incompletion directed toward Wilson was an end zone target late in the fourth quarter, a miss that would have salvaged a usable fantasy outing for the veteran receiver. Wilson was responsible for nearly one third of the total offensive output from a Cardinals offense that was held to under 200 yards by the stingy Seattle defense, finishing second on the team in targets behind the eight of tight end Trey McBride. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of another difficult test against the Rams in Week 10.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier rushed 17 times for 46 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, gaining zero additional yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

In what was the first game as the clear starter for the Cardinals in the absence of both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight, Allgeier was contained to only 2.7 yards per carry as the offense managed under 200 yards of total offense against the stingy Seattle defense. Fantasy managers that were quick to scoop Allgeier off of waivers heading into Week 9 are surely to be disappointed with the returns, particularly considering Knight had largely outperformed the former prior to missing Week 9 with a concussion. Expect a near-even split backfield once Knight returns, which appears likely to be in Week 10 when the Cardinals face another difficult test in the Rams.

item.title: Gardner Minshew completed 21-of-30 passes for 166 yards in the Cardinals’ 17-3, Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, adding four yards on one carry.
item.description:
Gardner Minshew ARI Quarterback
